name: Can I add an island to a small custom kitchen without making it feel cramped?

mainEntity.name: Can I add an island to a small custom kitchen without making it feel cramped?
mainEntity.text: Can I add an island to a small custom kitchen without making it feel cramped?

acceptedAnswer.text: A small kitchen can include an island only if the layout allows enough clearance around it for safe movement and everyday use. The key issue is not just whether the island fits on paper, but whether people can open appliance doors, stand at the sink, and pass through the kitchen comfortably. In many smaller Los Angeles homes, a full island can make the room feel tighter unless it is carefully scaled. A narrower island, a peninsula, or a built-in prep counter may deliver better function with less crowding. The design should account for seating overhang, trash pullouts, corner access, and traffic between the sink, stove, and refrigerator. If the kitchen is being redesigned from scratch, the safest approach is to test multiple layout options before committing. A custom design team can model whether the island improves storage and workflow or simply takes up valuable floor space.
acceptedAnswer.description: A small kitchen can sometimes fit an island, but only if circulation clearances, appliance doors, and work zones still function properly. If the island blocks traffic or reduces walkway space, a peninsula or movable prep surface may work better.
